title: The Simeon brothers and the Chicago cabarets young clarinetists haunted
summary: Omer Simeon started clarinet in Chicago; the young clarinet players went to the Royal Garden, Dreamland and other cabarets to hear Oliver, Noone and others.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: So really Omar Simeon Elmer Simeon, he wasn't a clarinet player when he came from New Orleans.
No, I think he started in Chicago.
Because his brother used to play the violin. I think they both -- I think they came when they were young kids.

Very quiet fellow. Both of them Simeons are play, Simeon, a very beautiful fellows. We used to hang out at the -- we clarinet players -- every night we could, we'd put on long pants and go in the cabaret, like the Royal Garden, where Joe Oliver was Earl Gardner, Oliver Willis and like Jimmy Noonan and Ed Beckstrom. Dave Brady had the band at the Dreamland. We used to go to all of them -- (unintelligible) fellows. learn from all those
Yeah. Well, I mean the thing is at that time that you're talking of the kind of jazz people in Chicago were influenced very much by these guys from Chicago, from and New Orleans.
